author: sonnet
label: c2-seed-sonnet-01
changes: Expanded the terse sketch into a self-explanatory document: setup, targets, a component table, and numbered step descriptions that say what triggers each step.
Explained what the pieces are, including WAL, replay lag, and the control store, which is a new component the original never defined.
Defined the active-region record and where it lives: a strongly consistent store outside Region A, with an epoch and leases, so fencing works when A is unreachable and its own code stops writing.
Moved the lag check before fencing so that stopping on lag leaves everything unchanged, and showed the stop and override paths in the flowchart.
Specified that B's workers start only after the job fix-up, once the database is writable, and that DNS switches only after B is scaled and healthy.
Described what happens to jobs that were running in A: they are reset to pending, may run twice and so need idempotency, and some may be lost within the RPO.
Added failed and interrupted run handling: resume, abort allowed only before promotion, roll-forward after promotion, and a health-check failure path in the flowchart.
Added the post-return behaviour of A, including the fencing epoch, the database rebuild, and a separate planned failback.
Defined jargon on first use: RPO, RTO, WAL, epoch, warm standby, fencing, TTL.
Reworded the opening setup so the lag mechanism reads in a clear sequence.
Stated that each step starts when the previous one finishes, and removed the awkward per-step 'triggered when' phrasing.
Clarified that the lock is released when the lag check stops the run, in both the diagram and the notes.
Made abort precise: it sets the record back to A with a higher epoch, and on-call chooses to abort.
Moved lock release into step 9 and noted that a failed health check keeps the run at step 7.
Tightened wording in the components table and the lease and fail-closed bullets.
Added a one-line definition of fencing up front so later uses are clear.
Merged the two lag-check arrows into the same node in the diagram into one labelled edge, removing a duplicated path.
Reworded the lease bullet so it says exactly when writing is allowed and why a partitioned A stops (it cannot renew).
Changed 'Abort before step 4' to 'Abort during steps 1 to 3' and 'After step 4' to 'From step 4 on', removing ambiguity about step 4 itself.
Added what on-call does when abort is refused (resume the failover).
Clarified that the override means starting a new run rather than continuing the stopped one.
Removed the redundant 'record (fencing and who may write)' phrasing in the record section.
